title: Theatre of Decay
summary: A video game that started as a university course project and grew into a full itch.io release.
description: Theatre of Decay began as a project for a course at Linköping University and grew from there into a complete, published game. Built with Godot and GDScript, it was developed by two friends, taking the project from a coursework prototype through iteration, playtesting, and polish to a public release on itch.io.

title: ragnar
summary: An open-source, production-ready RAG pipeline for financial data, built as a reusable Go library.
description: During a summer internship at Modular Finance, I was responsible for engineering an end-to-end retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline tailored for processing financial data in production. I architected the solution as a reusable Go library to enable seamless integration into LLM-based agent workflows and other internal projects. The work resulted in an open-source release, ragnar, allowing instant RAG integration into any Go application.

title: Open-Love
summary: Basically Lovable, but open-source and self-hosted — describe a project and watch it get built iteratively.
description: Open-Love is an AI-powered site builder: basically Lovable, but open-source and self-hosted. Users describe what they want through a chat interface and watch the project get built turn by turn, with full project history and a live preview kept up to date throughout. It generates everything from plain static sites to full React/NestJS applications, guided by customizable design references, and ships a built-in content manager so editable sections — products, posts, testimonials, and the like — can be updated afterward without regenerating the project. It also supports reference materials like images, PDFs, and text files to steer generation, and offers two builder backends: Claude Code by default, and a fully local, free Ollama option. Built with a NestJS backend and a React/TypeScript frontend, released under the MIT license.
